messages:
incident-bot: Detected canary anomaly: canary group 'wave-72' showing elevated 5xx + probe flaps (service=api-serving, region=us-east-1). Auto-pager: current oncall. Alert: https://metrics.internal/redwood/api-serving/wave-72 | Rule: canary-5xx-spike

eric_oncall: on it, dialing in. please post quick summary of observed failures.

joy_sre: summary: spike began ~23:02 UTC. 5xx + readiness toggles on ~6 of 12 canary instances. Errors appear correlated with higher concurrency on a particular model shard. Logs show repeated resource allocation failures followed by upstream 502s.

ana_deploy: we increased canary weight from 5% -> 25% at ~22:50 to speed validation for burst behavior. rollouts used feature flag: canary_wave_72. nothing flagged in CI.

eric_oncall: is automated rollback kicking? if not, prefer kill-switch first to stop customer impact.

incident-bot: Policy check: automated rollback window expired due to manual gating config (requires 10m stable). Manual action advised.

joy_sre: health endpoints: readiness fell to 60% then recovered briefly, liveness stable. sample log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T23:03:12Z ERROR runtime: alloc failure: kv-cache reserve failed - insufficient memory
2026-03-15T23:03:13Z ERROR router: request handler crash -> 502
2026-03-15T23:03:14Z WARN probes: readiness returned 500
```

ana_deploy: can flip flag in LaunchDarkly. command I use: 
```
ldctl toggle --flag canary_wave_72 --env prod --off --actor deploy-bot
```
I can do it now. alternatives: trigger full rollback deploy which may take longer.

eric_oncall: execute flag now. Lina, prep customer comms for US-EAST degraded generation. Omar, get CS ready for inbound reports.

lina_prod: drafting: "We are aware of elevated errors affecting model generation for customers in US-EAST following a canary rollout. We have disabled the canary and are monitoring. We will provide an update within 30 minutes with root cause and expected resolution." posting to status in 5m unless we need to shorten.

omar_cs: I'll queue templated replies and set priority for any P0 customers.

ana_deploy: RUN: ldctl toggle --flag canary_wave_72 --env prod --off --actor deploy-bot -> success. Propagation TTL ~30s.

eric_oncall: watching dashboards. 5xx dropping already. good.

incident-bot: Action recorded: manual flag disable by ana_deploy at 23:05:09 UTC.

joy_sre: healthcheck success back ~97% across pool. 5xx rate trending to baseline. collecting heap profiles and performance traces to s3://incidents/3602234567/. initiating post-incident trace capture.

lina_prod: publishing customer message now. content: "Resolved: canary disabled, traffic reverted to stable pool; monitoring. Follow-up to include RCA and mitigation steps."

omar_cs: posted to affected customers and internal ops. few customers reported short-lived degraded responses; no data loss.

eric_oncall: status: paging -> mitigated. assign RCA owners: joy_sre + ana_deploy. ETA 4 hours for initial findings. Zoe, handoff to you at 23:30. leave outstanding items here.

zoe_next_oncall: taking handoff at 23:30. open actions I see: 1) confirm no residual canary instances in us-east (verify service discovery). 2) verify stable QPS and p50/p95 latency baselines. 3) ensure heapdumps and logs are uploaded. 4) prep brief for postmortem meeting.

joy_sre: confirmed: artifacts uploaded to s3://incidents/3602234567/ - logs, profiles, and supporting dashboards. preliminary hypothesis: quantized memory path under concurrent prefix loads leads to transient allocation failures in the KV cache; will instrument and repro in staging.

eric_oncall: thanks. closing live incident page. continue investigation in this thread and schedule postmortem. :white_check_mark:
